title: The beta pitch and the waitlist survey
description:
**Phase 1 of 5.** Nothing blocks it. Runs in parallel with the cross-account provisioning epic.

The top of the funnel: a third CTA on the marketing home page, a /beta pitch page, and an unauthenticated survey that writes one waitlist record.

**No sign-in anywhere in this epic.** Nothing behind the survey needs an identity yet, and an auth wall in front of a form is the most reliable way to lose the top of a funnel. Authentication appears exactly once in this initiative, at checkout, where it is a formality. The work email field comes first and saves on blur, so an abandoned survey still leaves a lead.

The pitch page states four costs together — the floated $19.95 monthly fee, AWS billed to the customer, model tokens billed to the customer, and the one-time setup fee. This is not a disclosure nicety. A page that floats $19.95 and leaves the other three implicit measures what people will pay for a $19.95 thing and then watches them churn when the AWS bill lands, which reads as demand and is not.

The survey is nineteen questions across three blocks: fit, AWS readiness, and price. That is longer than ideal and it is the right call, because the AWS block disqualifies people who could never be customers. Expect a lower completion rate and treat where people drop as a market finding rather than a form problem.

**Start with:** the public waitlist endpoint. Everything else on the page is copy, and copy can move while the record shape settles.

comments.text: After chatticus-3926bc: pitch page, survey form, and CTAs are Chattic.us-web. Waitlist HTTP (`c7c7c1` and related) remains in this repo until `574e4b` moves the store. Do not add `/beta` routes here.
